📖 Solomon's Contradictions — Rabbi Tanḥum's homily on why Kohelet seems to praise the dead over the living
👑 David's Forgiveness — the Temple gates that would not open until 'remember the good deeds of David'
⚰️ How David Died — the Angel of Death, the broken staircase, and Solomon's question about the corpse and the dogs

overview.title: 📖 Overview: David's Death, Kohelet's Contradictions, and Hillel's Patience
overview.subtitle: Shabbat 30a–30b
overview.hebrewSource: לְעוֹלָם יְהֵא אָדָם עַנְוְותָן כְּהִלֵּל וְאַל יְהֵא קַפְּדָן כְּשַׁמַּאי
overview.label: The scene:
overview.text: Having established in the mishna that a lamp may be extinguished for a critically ill person, the Gemara asks why the mishna phrases this case as 'exempt' rather than 'permitted,' and works out that it is describing a case of mortal danger while stylistically mirroring the liable clause. This opens an extended aggadic detour: Rabbi Tanḥum is asked whether one may extinguish a lamp for a sick person, and answers with a sweeping homily reconciling apparent contradictions in Solomon's own words about life and death, tracing King David's forgiveness for his sin, the Temple dedication, and the story of David's death while studying Torah on Shabbat. The Gemara then explains why the Sages nearly suppressed the books of Ecclesiastes and Proverbs due to internal contradictions, and closes the daf with the famous teaching that one should be patient like Hillel, not impatient like Shammai — introducing test cases about to be told.

slides.title: 🛌 Reading the Mishna's 'Exempt' Carefully
slides.subtitle: Two levels of illness, two different rules

nodes.content: ❓ The mishna says one who extinguishes a lamp for a sick person is 'exempt' — but if the illness is life-threatening, shouldn't it say 'permitted'?
✅ Answer: the mishna IS about mortal danger, and it truly is permitted ab initio — 'exempt' is used only for stylistic match with the liable clause that follows
⚖️ Contrast: Rabbi Oshaya's baraita (not life-threatening, so he may not extinguish ab initio, but if he did, he is exempt) follows Rabbi Shimon's view — a different, non-dangerous case

slides.title: 📖 Rabbi Tanḥum Resolves Solomon's Contradictions
slides.subtitle: Why Kohelet seems to praise death over life

lines.speaker: Question
lines.text: May one extinguish a lamp before a sick person on Shabbat?

lines.speaker: R' Tanḥum
lines.text: Solomon, where is your wisdom? Your father David said 'the dead praise not the Lord' — yet you said 'I praised the dead more than the living,' and also 'a living dog is better than a dead lion'!

lines.speaker: Resolution 1
lines.text: David meant: engage in Torah before death, since the dead are idle from mitzvot. Solomon's praise of 'the dead' refers to the righteous forefathers, whose merit outlasts any living king's decree.

lines.speaker: Resolution 2
lines.text: 'A living dog is better than a dead lion' teaches that life itself is preferable — as shown by Solomon's own dilemma when David died and lay exposed.

lines.speaker: Conclusion
lines.text: A lamp is called נֵר, and a person's soul is also called נֵר — better to extinguish an ordinary lamp than to endanger the lamp of a human soul.

slides.title: 👑 David: Sin, Forgiveness, and Death
slides.subtitle: Three linked episodes
rows: God forgives his sin but says the forgiveness will be made known only in Solomon's lifetime, not David's
They would not open for the Ark until Solomon said 'remember the good deeds of David Your servant' — then fire descended and all Israel knew David was forgiven
He studied Torah every Shabbat to keep the Angel of Death at bay; the Angel shook the garden trees, David went to look, the staircase broke, and in that pause of study he died

callout.label: Solomon's dilemma:
callout.text: David's body lay in the sun with hungry dogs nearby; the study hall advised placing bread or an infant on the body so it could be moved indirectly, since the dead may not be handled directly on Shabbat.

slides.title: 📜 Why Kohelet and Proverbs Nearly Vanished
slides.subtitle: The Sages' method for resolving apparent contradictions

steps.content: 1️⃣ The Sages sought to suppress (ginzu) the Book of Ecclesiastes because its statements seem to contradict each other

2️⃣ Kept because its beginning and end are Torah-true: 'what profit has man under the sun' (none — but before the sun, i.e. Torah, there is profit) and 'fear God and keep His mitzvot, for this is the whole man'
3️⃣ 'Vexation is better than laughter' vs. 'I said of laughter, praiseworthy': resolved as God's anger at the righteous now vs. His joy with them in the World-to-Come
4️⃣ The Book of Proverbs faced the same challenge — 'answer not a fool' vs. 'answer a fool': resolved as Torah matters (answer) vs. mundane matters (don't)

callout.label: Key teaching:
callout.text: The Divine Presence rests only amid the joy of a mitzva — not sadness, laziness, frivolity, or idle talk (Elisha needed a minstrel to restore his prophecy).

slides.title: 😌 Be Patient Like Hillel, Not Impatient Like Shammai
slides.subtitle: The Sages' baraita opens a new set of stories
slides.hebrewSource: לְעוֹלָם יְהֵא אָדָם עַנְוְותָן כְּהִלֵּל וְאַל יְהֵא קַפְּדָן כְּשַׁמַּאי
slides.label: The teaching:
slides.text: The Sages taught: A person should always be patient like Hillel and not impatient like Shammai. The Gemara introduces this principle with 'there was an incident involving two people' — setting up the famous stories (continued on the next daf) of would-be converts who tested Hillel's and Shammai's tempers with outrageous demands.

summary.principle: The mishna's 'exempt' for extinguishing a lamp before a dying person is really full permission, illustrated through Rabbi Tanḥum's aggadic tour of David's sin, forgiveness, and death, the Sages' near-suppression of Kohelet and Proverbs over apparent contradictions, and the opening teaching that one must be patient like Hillel.

flowSteps.content: 🛌 Mishna's 'exempt' for a critically ill person really means fully permitted
📖 R' Tanḥum's homily: a soul is also called 'ner' — better to extinguish a physical lamp than risk it

columns.content: 👑 David forgiven for his sin, but only revealed in Solomon's time; died studying Torah on Shabbat
📜 Kohelet and Proverbs nearly suppressed for 'contradictions,' resolved through careful reading

flowSteps.content: 🎓 Key Principle: A person should always be patient like Hillel, and not impatient like Shammai

quiz.q: Why does the mishna use the word 'exempt' rather than 'permitted' for extinguishing a lamp before a critically ill person?
o: Because it is actually forbidden after the fact
Because it truly is permitted ab initio, but the mishna uses 'exempt' for stylistic consistency with the following clause about liability
Because the sick person must consent first
Because it only applies on Festivals
quiz.e: The Gemara explains that although the halakha is full permission for a life-threatening case, the mishna phrased it as 'exempt' to match the wording of the adjacent clause about liability.

quiz.q: According to Rabbi Tanḥum's homily, why is it permitted to extinguish a physical lamp to help a critically ill person?
o: Because lamps are not valuable
Because both a lamp and a person's soul are called 'ner,' and it is better to extinguish the lamp of flesh and blood than to endanger the lamp of God (the soul)
Because Shabbat laws do not apply to lamps
Because Solomon ruled this way explicitly
quiz.e: Rabbi Tanḥum concludes his homily by noting that both a physical lamp and a human soul are called 'ner,' so preserving the soul takes precedence over preserving the physical lamp.

quiz.q: According to the Gemara's account, what finally caused the Temple gates to open for the Ark during Solomon's dedication?
o: Solomon offering more sacrifices
Solomon saying 'remember the good deeds of David Your servant'
The Ark being carried by priests instead of Levites
Twenty-four days of silence
quiz.e: After Solomon's earlier prayers were unanswered, the gates opened only once he invoked David's merit, at which point fire descended and Israel knew David had been forgiven.

quiz.q: Why did the Sages nearly suppress the Book of Ecclesiastes?
o: Because it was written too late
Because its statements appeared to contradict each other
Because it never mentions God
Because Solomon was considered unreliable
quiz.e: The Gemara states the Sages considered suppressing Ecclesiastes because of its apparently self-contradictory statements, but kept it since its beginning and end are firmly rooted in Torah.

quiz.q: What baraita does the daf conclude with, setting up the following stories?
o: A person should always study alone
A person should always be patient like Hillel and not impatient like Shammai
A person should never argue about halakha
A person should follow Rabban Gamliel in all matters
quiz.e: The daf ends with the Sages' teaching that one should emulate Hillel's patience rather than Shammai's impatience, introducing an incident involving two people that continues onto the next daf.
